tasks.title: book/confirm transport from Hanoi to Cat Ba
suggestions: Cat Ba Express is the standard option: bus + speedboat combo from Hanoi to Cat Ba town, $11-15 one-way, ~3h15-3h30 total travel time. Book at https://catbaexpress.com/bus-hanoi-to-cat-ba.html or their office at 214 Tran Quang Khai St, Hoan Kiem (hotline/WhatsApp +84 84 824 4999).
Daily departures from Hanoi at 07:30, 10:45, and 14:00 — the 07:30 slot gets you to Cat Ba town by early-mid afternoon, matching your Old Quarter accommodation notes about the 12 Oct transfer.

Free hotel pickup is included ONLY for hotels inside the Old Quarter — confirms the same constraint noted on your Hanoi accommodation task, so book that hotel first and give its address when booking this transfer.

Alternative/comparison operators if Cat Ba Express is sold out: catbabus.com and catbaexpressbus.com both run similar bus+speedboat combos from ~$10.50; Bookaway (https://www.bookaway.com/routes/vietnam/hanoi-to-cat-ba-island) lets you compare several operators and times in one place.
Book a day or two ahead once your Hanoi hotel is confirmed — seats can sell out on the popular morning departure, especially in peak climbing season.

The cable car doesn't have single scheduled "departures" like a bus — it runs continuously, a cabin every ~10 minutes, during 09:00-11:00 and 13:00-17:00 (it closes for a lunch break 11:00-13:00, and is closed entirely on Tuesdays for maintenance). So there's no specific time to tell your friend to "catch" — just get to the station within opening hours.

Timing check for your group: the 10:45 bus from Hanoi to the cable car's mainland station (Dong Bai/Cat Hai) is roughly a 2-hour leg, so you'd likely arrive around 12:30-13:00 — right around the lunch reopening. Good news: this means there's a real chance you and your friend end up crossing around the same time despite arriving totally different ways.

Your friend (flight lands 11:20): transfer from Cat Bi Airport to the cable car's mainland station is about 28km / 30-40 min by taxi — fixed fares run roughly 100,000-200,000 VND (negotiate before getting in, or use Grab). That puts him at the station around 12:00-12:10, which is BEFORE the 13:00 reopening — so he'll have a short wait regardless of traffic, meaning he has buffer and doesn't need to rush off the plane.

Does he need to book ahead? Not strictly — tickets are sold at the counter too — but booking online is worth it to skip the queue and get a QR code straight to your phone, especially since he'll already be waiting around for the 13:00 reopening anyway.

Where to buy JUST the cable car ticket (no bus, since he doesn't need the Hanoi leg): the official Sun World ticketing site at https://booking.sunworld.vn — select Cat Ba, pick one-way or round-trip. This is separate from Cat Ba Express's bus+cable-car combo product, which is why you couldn't find a cable-car-only option on their site. Price: 50,000 VND one-way / 100,000 VND round-trip per person (~US$2-4) — cheap enough that the main benefit of booking ahead is skipping the line, not saving money.

tasks.title: Japan after Hanoi

noteItems.text: thinking of doing 22nd Oct to 29th of Oct trip from Hanoi to Tokyo.

Things I want to do: onsen, ramen robot cafe, half day nice walks/hikes, one or two nights in the best capsule hotel, find the best vegan places to eat, anime spots to visit/shop, nice affordable airbnb/place to stay for the rest of the nights, bouldering at b-pump ogikubo. some days I'll be travelling with my Japanese partner, some days she might go fabric shopping by herself or visit friends

E.VINO SPAGHETTI — Marunouchi Building B1F, 2-4-1 Marunouchi, Chiyoda-ku (11:00-22:30). A robot called P-Robo does the entire cook — boils/thaws, cooks, and even cleans its own pan — across 8 pasta dishes, ready in 45-75 seconds. Confirmed currently operating, run by Pronto Corp. CHEFFY at Gurunavi Foodhall WYE, Haneda Innovation City (Tenkubashi) — an autonomous robot serving ramen recipes licensed from famous/Michelin-affiliated restaurants in ~90 seconds. Also shows up at Pepper Parlor in Shibuya.

suggestions: Robot Restaurant/robot cafe: the original Shinjuku Robot Restaurant has been closed since COVID and repeated reopening attempts have stalled (still closed as of 2026) — drop it from the itinerary. Source: https://www.travelcaffeine.com/robot-restaurant-review/. Closest substitute is Avatar Robot Cafe DAWN (https://dawn2021.orylab.com/en/), staffed by robot avatars remotely operated by people with disabilities — different vibe (more meaningful than spectacle) but worth checking if it still appeals.

Capsule hotel: The Millennials Shibuya is the standout for a genuine high-tech capsule experience (reclining pod, personal projector, tablet controls, free coffee/tea 24h) — central Shibuya location. If you want something cheaper and more traditional-feeling, Anshin Oyado Shimbashi (right by Shimbashi Station) is a well-reviewed classic capsule option. Budget roughly ¥2,500-9,000/night depending on style. Source: https://trulytokyo.com/best-capsule-hotels-in-tokyo/

B-Pump Ogikubo bouldering: open Mon-Fri 12:00-23:00, weekends/holidays 10:00-22:00 (closed only New Year), 30 seconds from Ogikubo Station. Day pass ¥2,530 + a one-time ¥2,200 registration fee for first-timers (~¥4,730 total your first visit). Popular with foreign climbers and has English support, so no language barrier issue. https://english.pump-climbing.com/bpump/

Half-day hike: Mount Takao (599m) is the easiest fit — ~50 min from Shinjuku via Keio Line to Takaosanguchi. October is actually peak season there (Takao Momiji Festival starts late October), so expect crowds on Trail 1 (paved, cable car option, ¥490 one-way/¥950 return). For a quieter walk with the same autumn colours, take Trail 3 (Katsura Grove) instead — about 1hr up, less crowded. Source: https://tokyocheapo.com/entertainment/outdoors/mount-takao-day-trip-tokyo/

Onsen: since it is a day trip not an overnight, Hakone is the practical choice (Kusatsu is 2.5hrs each way, too far for a day). Hakone Yuryo is a dedicated day-use onsen facility (no overnight rooms, built for exactly this) — see options and prices at https://www.erikastravelventures.com/hakone-day-use-onsen/. Get there via the Odakyu Romancecar from Shinjuku (~85 min) — the Hakone Free Pass (¥6,100) covers transport around the area if you want to combine it with sightseeing (Owakudani, the pirate ship on Lake Ashi) rather than just the bath.

Vegan food: T's Tantan (vegan tantan ramen, one location right at JR Tokyo Station B1F, super convenient) is the easiest one to just drop into. For a sit-down proper meal, the vegan restaurant in Jiyugaoka (Japanese vegan cuisine — katsu, soba, vegan eel, bento) is well reviewed. Komeda IS in Ginza is a good option if you want an all-vegan breakfast/brunch spot. Full list: https://www.happycow.net/best-vegan-restaurants/tokyo-japan

Anime spots/shopping: not researched in detail yet (no source to cite), but the two obvious anchors are Akihabara (electronics + anime/manga stores, figures, maid cafes) and Nakano Broadway (more curated/vintage collectibles, less touristy than Akihabara) — worth deciding which vibe you want since they are quite different; happy to dig into specific stores if you tell me what you are actually shopping for (figures, manga, retro games, cosplay, etc).

⚠ Nippori Fabric Town for your partner's solo shopping days — flagging this came from general knowledge, not a web search I actually ran, so treat it as unverified until I (or you) confirm it's still the right spot and check current opening hours/access before relying on it.

tasks.title: think up contract for new housemate so they can't stay over the test period
suggestions: Drafted a trial-period housemate agreement below — the key clause for your concern is #4 (no automatic continuation past the test period without both of you confirming in writing). This is a plain mutual-understanding document, not a legal lease, but it is the kind of thing Australian share-house arrangements commonly use to set expectations and it gives you a clean, agreed exit point if it does not work out.

--- DRAFT: Housemate Trial Period Agreement ---

1. Parties & dates: [Your name] and [housemate's name], trial period from [start date] to [end date] (recommend 4-6 weeks — long enough to know if it works, short enough that a bad fit does not drag on).

2. Rent & bond during trial: [amount] per week, due [day]. Bond of [amount] held by [you / a bond authority] — specify whether it is refundable in full if either party ends the trial early through no fault of the other.

3. House rules reference: trial is conditional on following the existing house rules (chores, guests, noise, shared costs) — attach or list them so there is no ambiguity about what "working out" means.

4. End of trial — THE KEY CLAUSE: the trial period ends automatically on [end date]. Continuing to live in the property after that date requires a NEW, separate written agreement signed by both parties. Silence, continued rent payment, or having moved belongings in does not extend the trial or create an ongoing tenancy — this is the line that stops someone just staying on by default.

5. Early exit: either party may end the trial early with [7-14] days written notice (text/email counts), no reason required. Bond handling on early exit specified in clause 2.

6. Not a substitute for a lease: if you decide to continue after the trial, you will both sign a proper share-house agreement or add them to the lease/bond at that point — this document only covers the test period.

One thing worth deciding before you finalize: what specifically counts as bond-forfeiting behaviour vs. a no-fault early exit (e.g. property damage vs. just personalities not clicking) — spelling that out in clause 2 avoids a dispute later if the trial ends badly.

⚠ Not legal advice — for actual bond handling and tenancy-law specifics in your state, a quick check against your state's residential tenancies authority (e.g. Fair Trading / Consumer Affairs) is worth doing before you both sign, especially around bond lodgement rules if any money changes hands formally.

claudeNotes.text: ✓ Actioned 2026-09-23: drafted a full trial-period housemate agreement (dates, rent/bond, house rules reference, early-exit terms, and the key clause that stops the trial silently becoming permanent) — see suggestions. Flagged that it is not legal advice and to sanity-check bond rules against your state's tenancy authority before signing.

noteItems.text: is this a good one to buy and what else might i need. ideally i want it to be able to run quietly too.

suggestions: On the AOOSTAR AG03 you photographed: reviews are mixed specifically on the quiet requirement. The manufacturer claims 38-45dB, but real owner reports (egpu.io forum review) describe an audible whine/hum under load that varies with GPU power draw — not silent. If quiet operation is a hard requirement, reviewers point to the AOOSTAR EG02 as a quieter alternative worth comparing before buying. Sources: https://egpu.io/forums/thunderbolt-enclosures/my-review-for-the-aoostar-ag03-thunderbolt-5-egpu-dock/ and https://vortexgaming.io/en/postdetail/913708

What else you need: (1) the GPU card itself — NOT included, AG03 is dock+PSU only; (2) a Thunderbolt 4/5 or USB4 certified cable — usually included with the dock, but if buying separately make sure it says "Thunderbolt-certified", not just USB-C, since a generic cable will bottleneck or fail to work; (3) confirm your laptop actually has a Thunderbolt/USB4 port that supports eGPUs (not all USB-C ports do, check your laptop's spec sheet); (4) GPU drivers from Nvidia/AMD once connected. Good news: since the AG03 has a built-in 800W PSU, you skip all the DIY power-cable wiring (24-pin, 8-pin PCIe) that a bare enclosure+separate-PSU build needs — it's much closer to plug-and-play.

✅ Also fixed the two bugs you flagged: the Add button was overflowing off-screen at narrower widths (form now wraps properly), and file uploads now accept PDFs too (not just images) with an actual preview + remove button instead of the cramped native "No file chosen" text.

Links for the additional items: the Thunderbolt 5 cable is actually INCLUDED in the AG03 box (80cm TB5 cable ships with the dock) — you don't need to buy one separately, confirmed via https://www.geeky-gadgets.com/aoostar-ag03-egpu-review/ and https://minixpc.com/products/aoostar-ag03-egpu-dock-with-oculink-usb4-v2-0-ports-compatible-with-thunderbolt-5. Buy the dock itself on Amazon (https://www.amazon.com/AOOSTAR-Thunderbolt-Supports-Mainstream-Graphics/dp/B0H2GJVXPL, ~$260-270) or direct from AOOSTAR (https://aoostar.com/products/aoostar-ag03-egpu-dock).

GPU card (not included in the dock) — for your quiet requirement, the ASUS Dual GeForce RTX 5060 Ti 16GB OC Edition tested under 30dBA under load with 0dB idle fan-stop (silent at idle), per https://whoismcafee.com/best-quiet-graphics-cards/. Buy on Amazon: https://www.amazon.com/ASUS-DisplayPort-2-5-Slot-Axial-Tech-Technology/dp/B0F4DVKSZ4 (~$429-480) or Newegg: https://www.newegg.com/asus-dual-rtx5060ti-o16g-geforce-rtx-5060-ti-16gb-graphics-card-double-fans/p/N82E16814126798. The non-Ti ASUS Dual RTX 5060 OC is a cheaper option that tests similarly quiet if 16GB isn't needed.

To confirm your laptop's port will actually run this dock: Win+X → Device Manager → look under "System devices" for a "Thunderbolt" or "USB4 Host Router" entry — if present, you're good. Or look up your exact laptop model's spec sheet on the manufacturer's site under Ports/Connectivity for "Thunderbolt 4/5" or "USB4". Guide: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/answers/questions/2288227/how-can-i-tell-if-i-have-thunderbolt-ports-and-wha

tasks.title: what are the best ways to learn a language? e.g. Japanese
suggestions: Best-fit approach for you specifically: you have a Japanese partner (per your Japan trip task) and a Tokyo trip 22-29 Oct — that's a built-in native speaker most learners don't have, so prioritize actually speaking over app-hopping. Structure: (1) hiragana + katakana first, 1-2 weeks, non-negotiable foundation; (2) layer in a kanji/vocab tool + a grammar resource; (3) use your partner (and/or italki) for real speaking practice rather than staying app-only.

Apps by purpose — rotate tools as your bottleneck changes rather than sticking to one forever: Duolingo (https://www.duolingo.com/course/ja/en/Learn-Japanese) is a fine on-ramp for absolute beginners but not sufficient alone; Anki (https://apps.ankiweb.net/) for free spaced-repetition vocab (~1,000 free Japanese decks available); WaniKani (https://www.wanikani.com/) for structured kanji + vocab (paid subscription); Bunpro (https://bunpro.jp/) for grammar from N5 through N1; italki (https://www.italki.com/) to book a real tutor for speaking practice; HelloTalk (https://www.hellotalk.com/) for casual language exchange with native speakers.

Free video resources if you'd rather not pay for anything at first: YouTube channels Japanese Ammo with Misa, Cure Dolly (grammar explained in an unusually clear way), and Kaname Naito all have hundreds of hours of free lessons.

Tied to your trip: 4 weeks of hiragana/katakana + basic conversational phrases before 22 Oct would get you reading menus/signs and using basic Japanese with your partner's friends/family during the trip — a concrete, achievable target given the timeline.
